title: Governance and compliance in Microsoft Fabric

claims.text: Fabric organizes its governance surface into four functional areas: managing the data estate (admin portal, domains, workspaces, capacities, metadata scanning), securing and protecting data (sensitivity labels, DLP, auditing), encouraging discovery and trust (OneLake catalog, endorsement, tags, lineage), and monitoring activity (monitoring hub, capacity metrics, admin monitoring workspace).

Domains let organizations logically group Fabric content by business area or department, enabling each department to apply its own governance settings where those settings have been delegated from the tenant level. Domains can contain subdomains, and workspace content can be filtered by domain in the OneLake catalog.

Governance settings in Fabric operate in a three-tier hierarchy: tenant-wide defaults set by Fabric admins, domain-level overrides applied by domain admins for delegated settings, and workspace-level controls managed by workspace owners for the most granular scope.

Capacities serve as isolation boundaries for compute resources and chargebacks, and the recommended practice is to split capacities by environment stage (development, test, acceptance, production) to achieve workload isolation and cost attribution.

Metadata scanning exposes a set of admin REST APIs (the scanner APIs) that external cataloging tools can call to retrieve item-level metadata across all Fabric items, including item name, ID, sensitivity label status, and endorsement status.

Sensitivity labels from Microsoft Purview Information Protection can be applied to Fabric items manually or automatically through mechanisms such as default labeling, label inheritance, and programmatic labeling. Labels persist on data even when it is exported via supported export paths.

Purview DLP policies for Fabric automatically scan DLP-supported item types on upload to detect sensitive information, generate audit log entries for every detection, and can surface configurable alert messages to data owners when proprietary content is found.

Data-level security controls (row-level, column-level, and table-level) are available beyond workspace-role-based access, and currently these granular controls are supported specifically for SQL analytics endpoints, warehouses, Direct Lake, and KQL Database items.

Endorsement provides two levels of item trustworthiness signaling: item owners can self-apply Promoted status, while organizations can apply Certified status to items that meet defined quality standards. Endorsed items receive priority placement in certain search results and catalog views.

The OneLake catalog provides a single searchable surface for all Fabric items a user has access to, supporting domain-based filtering and tag-based filtering to help users reach relevant content without needing prior knowledge of which workspace or system holds the data.

Purview Data Map can scan Fabric items to extract item-level metadata and lineage, exposing that metadata via Atlas APIs for external services. A live view lets data consumers browse all Fabric workspaces they have viewer access to directly within Purview; manual scanning for full item-level metadata is available at the enterprise tier.

Microsoft Fabric holds multiple compliance certifications including HIPAA BAA, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27017, ISO/IEC 27018, and ISO/IEC 27701. Some advanced governance capabilities (Purview Information Protection, Purview DLP, and cross-org Purview governance) require licensing beyond the base Fabric license.
